prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The starting network learned to pick DONE immediately in every episode: 0 placements and 0 success. The untrained trace shows why. Each action's column is mirrored: a brick anchored at column x fills columns X-dx-x to X-1-x, while rows match. For example, "1x1 at row 7, col 2" filled column 5, and "1x2 at row 7, col 6" filled columns 0 and 1. The placement head reads features at the anchor cell, but the brick lands at the mirrored column. So placement scores have almost nothing to do with their real outcome, nearly every placement looks negative, and DONE (reward 0) wins. Flipping the feature map along x before the footprint head lines the anchor up with the real footprint. Every candidate makes that fix. The second candidate also adds a head that knows where a brick lands, and the third uses fewer PPO epochs to get more samples.

### Round 2
The x-mirror fix in the placement head was the key change: dev success went from 0.00 to 0.75 (r1c1). With 2 PPO epochs (r1c3) it scored 0.73, but its seeds were 0.52 and 0.94. That is far more spread than the 0.02 gap between the two runs, so the networks have enough capacity and the outcome mostly depends on how fast and how reliably training goes. The r1c1 learning curve was still rising at the end, and the early phase where the agent just pressed DONE took about 25% of the budget, which also points to too few samples. The landing-aware head (r1c2, 0.53) cost more compute per sample, got fewer steps and did worse; it is not worth pursuing. Dev failures are mostly unfinished builds (few cells outside the target, IoU 0.92–0.96), and the traces show the agent stopping one brick short. So the DONE decision and longer-horizon credit are the next things to test, along with more samples (1 epoch).

### Round 3
The mirror fix took dev success from 0 to about 0.75, so the network's action layout must be checked against what the actions actually fill. After that, recipe changes did most of the work. More fresh samples helped: 1 epoch scored 0.86 and 2 epochs 0.73, though the two 2-epoch seeds were 0.52 and 0.94. A longer credit horizon (gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95) with 2 epochs scored best at 0.90. Head changes hurt: the landing-aware head scored 0.53 and the placement-aware DONE head 0.34, the latter with high seed variance. Remaining failures are a few wrong or missing cells (IoU 0.99), likely overhang ordering or stopping early. The training curve flattens late. Next tests: combine 1 epoch with the long horizon; add a dilated residual conv for wider spatial context; and try both together.

### Round 4
Flipping the features along x (the mirror fix) is what made learning possible. Fewer PPO epochs, and so more samples, helped: r2c1 used 1 epoch and scored 0.86 on both seeds. r2c3 (2 epochs, gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95) is the best at 0.90. All three round-3 failures got stuck in the same way. Each has a seed scoring 0.078, mean IoU 0.714 and 0 cells placed outside the target. They build only layer 0, never stack, then choose DONE. This early trap is a matter of seed luck, not of capacity. The 1-epoch long-horizon run (r3c1) reached 0.83 on its other seed. The dilated conv cut the step count and gave no clear gain. So with only 3 trials left, I make small changes to r2c3 aimed at avoiding the ground-only trap. One gives more exploration, one gives credit over whole episodes instead of value bootstrapping, and one stops the critic from interfering with the DONE decision.

## Trial it ended with
name: 2 epochs, longer credit horizon
hypothesis: Same network and 2-epoch recipe as r1c3, with gamma 0.99 and gae_lambda 0.95 instead of 0.95 and 0.9. Episodes run about 10 to 16 placements, so with gamma 0.95 the +1 for an exact build is heavily discounted at early steps. A longer horizon should give more credit to finishing exactly and less to stopping early. Refuted if dev success is no better than r1c3 (0.73) or if training becomes less stable.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
